# Rules parity probe (#1053, #1054)

**Generated by `tools/rules_parity_probe.py`; do not edit by hand.**

Duplication is measured statically by `tools/duplication_audit.py`. This document answers the question that decides whether a duplicate is *debt* or a *bug*: does each copy give the same answer for the same character?

The probe feeds every layer an identical character and compares output. A layer that cannot be called with a given spelling is itself the finding — an adapter that resolves the same save differently depending on which module asked is a defect regardless of the arithmetic.

## What this means for #1054

The architecture decision says **no engine owns a rule**. These results show the stronger problem: the rule is owned by four places at once, and they do not agree on how to be called. Consolidating them is not a refactor for tidiness — until it happens, "the CWN save rule" is not a single fact in this codebase.

The arithmetic agreeing (where it can be compared at all) is why this has survived: no test fails, because no test asks two layers the same question. That is what this probe adds.
